name: Nosaxa
description: A star 90 parsecs away, 2.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31895: radius 2.143 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 4.032 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.049) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31895: effective temperature 5591 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 4.02 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 8 published values span log g 3.92 to 4.09, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31895: distance 89.767 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.019), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 90 parsecs away, 2.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 4.032 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,591 K, so 2.143 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 31895: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 48265
quotes.card: HD 48265, also named Nosaxa, is a star in the southern constellation Puppis.
quotes.introduction: It has an apparent visual magnitude of 8.07, which makes it too faint to be seen with the naked eye.
